I will think this through the way I always do — same as last year, with small changes if something went wrong.

My land is 14 mu. The big piece, about 10 mu, is my wheat-maize ground. That land never rests — wheat in winter, maize in summer. Then I have a small piece, maybe 2 mu, where I put cotton, and another 2 mu for chili near the house where I can watch it and water it easy.

For wheat, I do what my husband's brother does and what the old people taught me. I buy compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, one bag (50 jin... I mean 50 kg) per mu before planting. Then in spring when wheat wakes up, I spread urea — about half a bag per mu. That is how everyone around here does it. If I put less, I am scared the wheat will be yellow and thin. Better to spend a few extra yuan on fertilizer than watch a bad harvest. I water wheat three times — once before winter, once at jointing when it stands up, once when it fills the grain. The well is close so water is not too expensive. I spray one time for aphids in spring, sometimes a second time if I see them bad.

For maize after wheat, I dig the stubble in with the rotary machine the man brings. I put one bag compound as base and one bag urea when maize is knee-high. Maize does not need much water if the summer rain comes, but I give it one irrigation if July is dry. I buy hybrid maize seed from the dealer in town — the Zhengdan type or whatever he recommends that year. My neighbors get 600 kg per mu in a good year, so I hope for that.

Cotton is more trouble. I plant Bt cotton seed — no one plants old cotton anymore because bollworm eats it up. Cotton wants more potash so I add some extra. I spray cotton maybe 4-5 times for bugs, even with Bt. Cotton is tiring but the price is okay some years.

Chili near the house — that one I fuss over. I put manure from my sister's pig and extra fertilizer. I water by hand or small pipe many times. Chili can pay well if the price is good at market. I pick many times through autumn.

I am 56. My knees hurt. My son works in town, only comes to help at wheat harvest and maize planting. So I hire the machine man for tillage and the combine at harvest. I cannot do heavy work alone anymore.
